findings.reason: the plan's locked decision and its section give opposite instructions for the same deliverable, so the node lands the wrong interface unless the decision is re-chosen (flag-only) or §6 is reverted.
findings.text: the decision element `figure-reviewer-writes` carries `data-choice="caption-only"` with a rationale that "the caption is the exception", but §6 (:2532) says the reviewer "reports defects and writes nothing" and defers caption writing ("Letting the reviewer write the caption, as this section first proposed, waits until the read-only review has been measured"), and the s6 comment at :2993 agrees ("The reviewer is read-only for now") — a builder of §6 reading the decisions block implements caption writing and then fails §6's own done-when, which requires "the composed brief states each figure rule above and that the reviewer writes nothing" (:2563)

findings.reason: one gate cannot prove three separate behaviours, and each half could land or fail independently, so the node should be split the way §14 and §17 were.
findings.text: §18 under one section header declares three independent deliverables with independent verdicts: `crew complete` refusing an undisposed blocking figure finding (promotion_checks.py), the repair reflex resuming the worker on a figure finding (repair.py), and run reviews no longer superseding one another across subjects (review_lifecycle.py), as its own "The read" and "The hazard" blocks and four write paths (:2637) show

findings.reason: §6's declared relationship omits a section its own mechanism and gate depend on, so a reader of the node graph sees §6 gated on evidence from a section it does not declare.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` wires `s6` only to `a-review-can-see-the-figure#s10`, but §6 (:2538) takes its lane from `_review_lane_candidates(config, profile="figure")`, "which `a-review-can-see-the-figure` §12 landed", and the gate `g-ssp-figure-review-lane` (:3359) requires `a-review-can-see-the-figure#s12` as its required evidence

findings.reason: the standalone scalar is read when the plan is scheduled and would have to be corrected (or the dependency removed) before the declaration matches what §6 does.
findings.text: `plan-standalone` states the plan "consumes no other plan's evidence and gates none", but §6 depends on and cites `a-review-can-see-the-figure` §10 and §12 and its gate `g-ssp-figure-review-lane` requires that plan's §12 as evidence

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited symbols resolve: `_review_lane_candidates(config, profile="figure")` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1442 has the `profile` keyword), `dispatch_review_for_run` (recovery_review_dispatch.py:1684), `TaskNode.images` (reckon/crew/node.py:754), `blocking_findings` (reckon/crew/repair.py:224), `crew dispose` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:618), and `select_profile_backend` is correctly stated as retired (absent from the tree).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §6 (:2559) and §18 (:2638) each name measurable outcomes and a declared negative control (the figure trigger removed; the figure review left out of the promotion read), both of which fail on the unfixed code.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 (:2566) and §18 (:2638) each require every log written under the run directory, starting with its revision and the literal command and ending in `EXIT=`, which is the durable path the earlier reviews asked for.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 and §18 name files and symbols by what they do (`figure_review.py`, `promotion_checks.py`, `test_a_blocking_figure_finding_holds_promotion.py`); no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers appear in the changed text.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the locked decision `figure-reviewer-writes` records `caption-only`, and its rationale defends caption writing, while §6 the section declares the reviewer writes nothing.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §18 states three independent behaviours across three modules (a promotion refusal in `promotion_checks.py`, a repair-reflex change in `repair.py`, and a supersede-separation in `review_lifecycle.py`) under one section and one gate.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §6's `depends-on` names only `a-review-can-see-the-figure#s10`, but §6's lane selection and its gate's required evidence come from `a-review-can-see-the-figure#s12` (plan meta :32), and the plan-level `plan-standalone` scalar still claims the plan consumes no other plan's evidence (:21).
